page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Left of the text, a column of small ornamental marks (») beside the lines, not text. No notes, no running head, and no printed catchword other than the word at the foot right.

main_text.p: est pro universis, per singulare sacramentum celebraretur in singulis. Poculum quippe immor-talitatis, quod confectum est de infirmitate nostra, & virtute divina, habet quidem in se, ut omnibus profit: sed, si non bibitur, non me-detur. Vel hinc manifestum est, quid sen-tiendum sit de caeteris. Similia haben-tur in responsione ad nonum caput ob-jectorum Gallorum Semipelagiano-rum; & sententia nona.

Eadem confusio sufficientiæ & effica-tiæ mortis Christi, Massiliensib. tribui-tur, in Epistola ejusdem ad Augustinũ, hisce verbis: Pro universo autē humano ge-nere (ajunt) mortuum esse Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum: & neminem prorsus a redem-tione sanguinis ejus exceptum, etiamsi omnem hac vitam alienissimâ ab eo mēte pertranseat, quia ad omnes homines pertineat divina mi-sericordiæ sacramentum: quo ideo plurimi non renoventur, quia, quod nec renovari utile habeant, praenoscantur. Itaque, quantum ad Deum attinet, omnibus paratam vitam ater-nam: quantum autem ad arbitrij libertatem, ab his tam apprehēdi, qui Deo sponte crediderint, & auxi-

page.notes: The small » marks in the left margin beside lines 1–10 and 14–25 are typographic line marks, not printed text, so they are left out. Doubtful readings: "autē" (line 14) and "mēte" (line 18) and "apprehēdi" (line 25) have a macron-like sign that may be a tilde; the marks are as seen. The page number is a decorative figure; read as 50. The catchword "& auxi-" is the start of the next page's first word, hyphenated at the foot.
